items.title: L’Italia è afflitta da vulnerabilità informatiche, senza una causa chiara
items.description: I ricercatori non riescono a spiegare del tutto perché le minacce informatiche in Italia siano così diverse rispetto a quelle di qualsiasi altro Paese.

items.title: North Korean Hackers Steal Developer Credentials to Inject Malware Into GitHub and Software Packages
items.description: A North Korea-aligned hacking group has moved beyond fake job interviews and now steals developer credentials to plant malware in trusted software projects. The group, tracked as DeceptiveDevelopment, used the stolen access to change code in public and private repositories between April and September 2026. items.description: Over 22.6 million exposed instances are potentially affected by the critical PHP flaws that have been targeted for over a week. The post PHP2Shell Attacks Root Palo Alto Firewalls but Fail Against WordPress appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: APT Hackers Use NetamLoader Malware to Target Windows 10 Systems in Asian Governments
items.description: A new malware framework called NetamLoader is being used against a custom version of Windows 10 that only government bodies in Asia use. The campaign looks like a supply-chain operation, and nobody has linked it to a known hacking group yet. The malware hides inside a Windows update package, borrows trusted software to run, and […] The post APT Hackers Use NetamLoader Malware to Target Windows…

items.title: Malicious Claude Code extension on Cursor planted SSH backdoors
items.description: A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor's extension marketplace for approximately 11 hours on October 29, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware designed to install persistent SSH backdoors. [...]

items.title: Aur0ra Ransomware Hackers Use Cursor AI Agents to Gain Domain Admin Access and Steal Data
items.description: Ransomware crews are now giving the hardest parts of a network break-in to AI coding tools. A group linked to Aur0ra ransomware used Cursor AI agents to go from stolen passwords to domain admin access, the highest level of control in a Windows network. From there, it collected data and prepared to deploy ransomware. The […] The post Aur0ra Ransomware Hackers Use Cursor AI Agents to Gain Domain…

items.title: Hackers Build Fake Polymarket Platforms That Rig Trades and Block Cryptocurrency Withdrawals
items.description: Criminals are copying the look of Polymarket, one of the biggest prediction market sites. They use the copies to take cryptocurrency from people who think they are placing real bets. Once a victim deposits money, the site decides every win and loss, and withdrawals stop working. The scams are not one-off websites. Three Russian-speaking “traffer” […] The post Hackers Build Fake Polymarket…

items.title: Undead Software Projects Continue to Raise Security Risks
items.description: A security firm patched a decade-old app to prevent the takeover of millions of machines, highlighting that abandoned domains remain a boon to attackers.

items.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
items.description: Flaws in SS7 and Diameter signaling protocols can allow attackers to track phone locations, intercept calls and SMS verification codes, and impersonate subscribers without compromising their devices. Cape explains how these attacks exploit trust between networks and how its security-focused mobile service helps defend against them. [...]

items.title: Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough.
items.description: As organizations eliminate passwords, attackers will adapt. Instead of attacking the authenticator directly, they will look for opportunities around it. The post Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough. appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.description: A Trezor Safe 5 hardware wallet bought from the reseller CryptoBilis has an extra circuit board that sends out the recovery phrase over a mobile network, a customer has reported. items.description: Ahmad Umar Agha, a Syrian Electronic Army hacker known online as "Th3Pr0," has been sentenced by a U.S. federal court to 42 months in prison for his role in a hacking conspiracy that targeted Western news outlets. items.title: As Russia's Cyberwar Evolves, Belarus Steps Forward
items.description: The "FrostyNeighbor" advanced persistent threat (APT) launched a destructive attack in Ukraine and is raising concerns about deeper alignment with Russian cyber objectives.

items.title: Hackers Actively Exploit Highly Critical Drupal Commerce Core Authorization Bypass Flaw
items.description: Drupal has warned that threat actors are exploiting a "highly critical" security flaw in its Commerce Core component. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-118539 (CVSS score: N/A), is a case of missing authorization affecting Commerce Core versions from 0.0.0 to 2.41 and from 3.0.0 to 3.3.13.
